note: Same word for leg and bridge; context tells which.

ex.en: My legs hurt from walking a long time.
I hurt my leg while working out.
Cross this bridge and the market is right there.

note: 바람이 불다 = the wind blows; 바람을 쐬다 = get fresh air.

ex.en: It's really windy today.
The wind is cold, so dress warmly.
Let's open the window and get some air.

note: Use Sino-Korean numbers: 일 층, 이 층.

ex.en: The restroom is on the second floor.
Our place is on the 10th floor.
Which floor are you going to? (in the elevator)
Please text me the address.
I wrote the wrong delivery address.
What's your email address?
Did you decide where to meet?
The wedding venue was really pretty.
This is a great place to take photos.
That tall building is our office.
This building doesn't have a parking lot.
The clinic is on the 3rd floor of the bank building.

en: to stop, park (a car); to make (plans)

ex.en: Driver, please stop here.
I parked the car in front of the house.
Have you made plans for summer vacation?

note: For feelings, use 마음 instead.

ex.en: My heart beats fast when I exercise.
Grandpa had heart surgery.

ex.s: 너무 놀라서 심장이 멈추는 줄 알았어요.
ex.en: I was so startled I thought my heart would stop.

note: Honorific for elders: 연세.

ex.en: Excuse me, but how old are you?
We're the same age.
You look young for your age.

note: Casual form of 이야기; 얘기하다 = to talk.

ex.en: Let's talk later.
Did you hear about that?
I talked with my friend until late at night.

en: to put against, touch; to park

ex.en: Please tap your card here.
Please don't touch the painting.
Where can I park the car?
Enjoy your vacation!
I enjoy cooking.
I enjoyed delicious food on the trip.
This phone has a great camera.
I don't know how to use the new feature.
This washing machine also has a drying function.
Which member of that group do you like?
A new member joined our soccer team.
I had dinner with my book club members.

note: 대화하다 = to have a conversation.

ex.en: Our family talks a lot together.
That person and I really click when we talk.
Having conversations in Korean is still hard.

note: 돌아가시다 also means to pass away (honorific).

ex.en: I have to go back home now.
I went back to work after vacation.
When are you going back to Korea?

en: to rise, go up; to climb
note: 르-irregular: 올라요, 올랐어요.

ex.en: Prices have gone up a lot lately.
My salary went up a little.
I climbed a mountain on the weekend.

en: to reduce, cut down, turn down

ex.en: I should cut down on coffee.
Please turn the volume down.
I cut back on eating out this month.
I work at a bank.
Our kid goes to elementary school.
I've been going to the gym lately.

note: An electric fan is 선풍기, not 팬.

ex.en: I'm a fan of that actor.
There were so many fans at the concert.
My dad is a baseball fan.

note: 치료하다 = to treat; 치료받다 = to get treated.

ex.en: I still have dental treatment left.
I'm getting treatment for my knee.
The puppy was sick, so it got treated at the vet.
I'm really interested in art.
My daughter goes to an arts high school.
Wow, this cake is practically a work of art!
This restaurant is famous for its cold noodles.
That person is very famous in Korea.
Famous tourist spots are always crowded.
My umbrella disappeared.
My headache went away after I took medicine.
The cat suddenly vanished, so I was worried.

note: Casual for 퍼센트; also short for 프로그램.

ex.en: All clothes are 30 percent off today.
Only 10 percent battery left.
My older brother is a pro golfer.
Open your mouth wide.
The food was so hot I burned my mouth.

ex.s: 이 음식은 제 입에 딱 맞아요.
ex.en: This food is exactly to my taste.

ex.s: 우리 집 앞에 큰 나무가 있어요.
ex.en: There's a big tree in front of our house.
It's fall, so the trees have turned red.
This dining table is made of wood.
Let's stop today's work here.
This task takes some time.
The home repair work finishes tomorrow.

note: Use Sino-Korean numbers: 삼 개월. Month names use 월.

ex.en: It's been 6 months since I started learning Korean.
Our baby is 8 months old now.
I signed up at the gym for 3 months.
Don't worry.
My mom worries about my health a lot.
I'm worried about the exam.
I watched a lot of cartoons as a kid.
These days I read comics on my phone.
Kids like animated movies.

ex.s: 비가 와요. 그래도 산책 갈 거예요.
ex.en: It's raining. I'm still going for a walk.
It's a bit pricey. Still, it's tasty.
I was tired, but I worked out anyway.
I'm dying to know the results.
If you have any questions, just ask.
I wonder how that movie ends.

ex.s: 본인 확인을 위해 신분증 보여 주세요.
ex.en: Please show your ID to verify your identity.

ex.s: 이 서류는 본인이 직접 오셔야 해요.
ex.en: You need to come in person for this document.
What do you yourself think?
Can you give me your phone number?
What's your waiting number?
Check the bus number carefully.
I watched a cooking video on YouTube.
I filmed a video of my kid's birthday.

ex.s: 그 영상 링크 좀 보내 주세요.
ex.en: Please send me the link to that video.

note: Used by females; males say 누나. Also for close older women.

ex.en: My older sister lives in Seoul.
Sis, let's eat this together.
My older sister sent me a wedding gift.
What animal do you like most?
I went to the zoo with the kids on the weekend.

ex.s: 이 아파트는 동물을 키울 수 있어요.
ex.en: You're allowed to have pets in this apartment.
Which direction is the subway station?
I took the bus going the opposite direction.
Go straight that way.
I'll send you the link.
This link won't open.
Tap the booking link to sign up.
These shoes fit perfectly.
I'll have just one drink.
It's exactly twelve o'clock.
The sky is really clear today.
I looked at the sky from the plane window.

ex.s: 하늘이 어두워요. 비가 올 것 같아요.
ex.en: The sky is dark. Looks like rain.

note: Always with a negative: 전혀 안, 전혀 몰라요.

ex.s: 저는 매운 음식을 전혀 못 먹어요.
ex.en: I can't eat spicy food at all.
I had no idea about that at all.
It's okay, it doesn't hurt at all.

note: 결정하다 = to decide.

ex.en: I still haven't made a decision.
We decided to move.
Did you decide what to order?
My brother and I have similar voices.
Do you have a color similar to this?
The two stores' prices are about the same.
I admit my mistake.
I'll admit that. You're right.
The company recognized my effort.

note: 계약하다 = to sign a contract.

ex.en: I'm signing the lease for the house next week.
My phone contract ends soon.
Read the contract carefully.

note: In everyday speech, 차 is more common.

ex.en: I bought a new car.
I changed my car insurance.
My son likes toy cars.
Please take a photo with the sea in the background.
I changed my phone wallpaper.
This drama is set in Busan.
I was born in Chicago.
When were you born?
My nephew was born last month.
Let's use less plastic for the planet.
I have a friend on the other side of the world.
My kid asked why the Earth is round.
Cross when the light changes.
The meeting time changed to three.
This neighborhood has changed a lot.
Your voice sounds off. Did you catch a cold?
It's nice to hear your voice on the phone.
That singer has a really nice voice.

note: Often a store promotion or a planned surprise.

ex.s: 이번 주에 커피 할인 이벤트를 해요.
ex.en: They're running a coffee discount promotion this week.
If you join the event in the app, they give you a coupon.
I planned a surprise for my husband's birthday.
I live alone.
I like traveling alone.
Did you eat all of this by yourself?
These cookies are star-shaped.
Did you change your hairstyle?
Same shape, but a different color.
My chest feels tight when I climb stairs.
I went to the hospital because of chest pain.
That movie warmed my heart.
Please say hello to your parents for me.

ex.s: 민호한테 이 말 좀 전해 줄래요?
ex.en: Could you pass this message on to Minho?
Please be sure to tell them congratulations.

note: Also means biography (different hanja).

ex.s: 이번 달 전기 요금이 많이 나왔어요.
ex.en: The electricity bill was high this month.
The power went out because of the typhoon.
Next time I want to buy an electric car.
I use a reusable cup to help the environment.
My company has a good work environment.
This is a good environment for raising kids.
The weather has been changing a lot lately.

ex.s: 이사 온 후에 생활에 큰 변화가 있었어요.
ex.en: My life changed a lot after moving here.
The new job is a good change for me.
I'm heading to the airport now.
I bought bread on my way home.

ex.s: 우리 집 창문은 남쪽을 향해 있어요.
ex.en: Our windows face south.

ex.s: 그 식당은 한 번 가 볼 가치가 있어요.
ex.en: That restaurant is worth a visit.
This watch has gone up a lot in value.
Family is worth more than money.
I played guitar in my college days.
I found photos from my childhood.
I miss those days.
Where is the store located?
I'll text you my location.
This hotel's location is really good.

note: Attached to nouns (형만큼); spaced after verbs (먹을 만큼).

ex.en: I'm as tall as my older brother.
Only take as much as you'll eat.
It wasn't as hard as I thought.

en: to go over, exceed; to be past

ex.en: It's already past ten.
My grandma is over ninety.
This bag is over 23 kilos.
Today's weather is perfect for a picnic.
Your Korean is almost perfect!
It's okay not to be perfect.
This used to be a café.
I'm much healthier than before.
Let's meet often like we used to.

note: 신경 쓰다 = to care, worry about.

ex.en: Don't worry about it.

ex.s: 요즘 일 때문에 신경이 많이 쓰여요.
ex.en: Work has been weighing on me lately.
A pinched nerve in my back makes my leg numb.

note: As a noun it means complex: 아파트 단지.

ex.en: I just asked because I was curious.
That's only a rumor.
I just need a little time.
Please recommend a good restaurant.
I really recommend this book.
The doctor recommended this medicine.

en: to collect, gather; to save up

ex.en: My son collects stickers.
Please gather the trash in one place.
I'm saving money for a trip.
That's my responsibility.
Having a dog is a big responsibility.
Who's in charge of this project?

note: 추가하다 = to add.

ex.en: Please add extra cheese.
Is there an extra charge?
I added my friend to the group chat.

note: ㄹ-irregular: 놀아요, 노는, 노세요.

ex.en: I hung out with friends on the weekend.
The kids are playing in the park.
Come over to my place.

en: to hold back, put up with

ex.en: Hang in there a bit. It'll be over soon.
I couldn't hold back my laughter.
I need the bathroom, but I'm holding it.

note: Used by females; males say 형. Also for close older men.

ex.en: My older brother is a good cook.
Oppa, are you free tomorrow?
I went to see a movie with my older brother.
I had a fight with my husband yesterday.
The kids are fighting over a toy.
Our team fought hard to the end.
Want to go see a baseball game this weekend?
My son is learning baseball.
Koreans really love baseball.
You already finished eating?
It's already Friday!
The plane has already arrived.

note: 최근에 = recently.

ex.en: I moved recently.
Do you have a recent photo?
What movie have you seen lately?
I'm making dinner right now.
Are you all ready for the trip?
I'm busy preparing for an interview.
Please send me the image file.
I looked up images online.
That actor has a really good public image.
Our team won!
My younger sibling beat me at the game.
Whoever wins rock-paper-scissors gets to choose.
You startled me!
I was surprised when I saw the price.
Don't be alarmed, it's me.
Could you explain it once more?
The doctor explained the test results.
It's hard to explain the directions.
I compared prices with another store.
Don't compare me with my older sister.
Compared to last year, it's much warmer.
Same here.
It's cold today, just like yesterday.

ex.s: 비싼 거나 싼 거나 맛은 마찬가지예요.
ex.en: Expensive or cheap, they taste the same.
I saw a celebrity at the airport!
That actor is the biggest star these days.
My daughter is the soccer star of her class.
It's suddenly raining.
My stomach suddenly hurts.
The call suddenly cut out while we were talking.
It's super hot today.
That restaurant is really good.
There were tons of people.
Light comes in through the window.

ex.s: 이 방은 빛이 잘 들어서 좋아요.
ex.en: This room gets good light, which I like.
The light is so strong it's blinding.
I'm in a meeting right now.
What time does the meeting start?
Today's meeting ran long.
I want to go to the beach this summer.
You can see the ocean from the hotel room.
Busan is nice because the sea is close.
Who's your favorite singer?

ex.s: 딸이 커서 가수가 되고 싶어 해요.
ex.en: My daughter wants to be a singer when she grows up.
I bought tickets to that singer's concert.
Did you book a hotel?
Hotel check-in is from three.
I stayed at a hotel near the airport.
How do you use this camera?
I took it with my phone camera.

ex.s: 여행 갈 때 카메라를 꼭 챙겨요.
ex.en: I always bring a camera when I travel.

note: 위험하다 = to be dangerous.

ex.en: It's dangerous, so don't run.
It's dangerous to walk around alone at night.
They say this surgery has almost no risk.
Take the elevator up to the 5th floor.
Shall we take the stairs up?
I climbed all the way to the top of the mountain.
